A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MUSEG research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and expanded supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MUSEG benchmark results, a preliminary shortcut study, reward ablations and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds a controlled GRPO comparison, hyperparameter experiments and general video QA evaluations.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-VL models, multi-segment training task, global/local matching rewards, timestamp and format rewards, and 400-step/500-step phased recipe remain unchanged. The newly supplied training prompt documents the procedure; it does not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix D expands evaluation from temporal grounding and time-sensitive understanding to general video QA on MVBench and Video-MME, including short, medium and long videos. Figure 2 also replaces an action-counting example with a temporal-ordering example. Existing training datasets and temporal benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds vanilla GRPO trained on the same data as MUSEG, providing an important controlled comparator. TRACE-7B newly participates in the THUMOS14, THUMOS15, Perception Test and E.T. Bench subset comparisons. The existing SFT baseline is renamed rather than replaced.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes the reported local-matching ablation protocol from 400 steps with timestamp reward to the complete 900-step MUSEG training process. Appendix B introduces a tuning protocol using 1,400 training samples and a 200-sample THUMOS evaluation subset. The main experiments retain their training schedule, splits and metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds sensitivity tests for reward weights alpha and beta, revises the existing local-matching ablation, and replaces Figure 2's bowl-counting case with an event-ordering case. Figure 7 drops the timestamp-reward diagnostic. The principal phased-reward analyses and Figure 4 case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Main MUSEG scores in Table 2 are unchanged, but v2 adds vanilla GRPO and TRACE results, replaces Table 3 results under the longer training protocol, and adds tuning and general-QA scores. Table 7 newly reports MUSEG scores of 67.4 on MVBench and 63.1 on Video-MME, versus 65.7 and 62.4 for the base model. Figure 2's qualitative outputs are replaced.

T1.justification: Reward definitions and the maximum-weight matching objective retain their mathematical substance. v2 expresses the bipartite graph using explicit weighted edge triples and moves the zero-score convention for empty matches into prose. These restate existing mathematics; no new theorem, proof or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: multi-segment grounding and timestamp-aware phased rewards improve temporal understanding and generalization to time-sensitive tasks. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new GRPO control as showing that multi-segment training data alone are insufficient, emphasizing the reward recipe's contribution. It adds the conclusion that general video QA performance is preserved and reframes the phased-reward explanation around stabilized reasoning and renewed exploration. The stated limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A and E newly disclose the exact training prompt, eight A100-80G GPUs, and per-phase training times for both model sizes. Appendix B documents reward-weight selection. Existing batch size, learning rate, token/frame limits, selected reward weights and project access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds recent video RL papers, including VideoRFT and VersaVid-R1, and more explicit contrasts with fixed CoT supervision and answer-only rewards. CoT, Qwen3 and the new evaluation benchmarks receive additional citations. The TRACE reference is removed even though TRACE remains an evaluated comparator.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites several preliminary and methodological explanations, gives format reward its own subsection, moves main-text baseline descriptions into Appendix C, and merges case studies into Main Results. Appendix organization, author information and citation style also change, while the overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different layout with a boxed full-width abstract, revised typography and relocated figures. Figure 2 is replaced, Figure 6 corrects the in-domain/out-of-domain color legend, and Figure 7 removes its timestamp series and secondary axis. Tables 5–8 are added, and Tables 3–4 gain average-score columns.

improvement.justification: The same-data GRPO control and full-schedule local-matching ablations strengthen attribution of gains to the reward design. Sensitivity tests, general-QA evaluations, the exact prompt and hardware timings improve validation and reproducibility. These provide a limited net improvement to the existing evidence, despite losing Figure 7's timestamp diagnostic and the TRACE citation.
